summary.headline: Gulshan Polyols Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR646 crore (+8% YoY) and EBITDA rose 135% to INR91 crore, a 14.2% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue of about INR646 crore was the highest quarterly turnover in company history, up 8% YoY. EBITDA of INR91 crore grew 135% YoY, with margin at 14.2% versus 6.5% a year earlier, and PAT of INR54 crore rose about 307% YoY. Ethanol was the main driver with an 18% segment EBITDA margin, while grain processing improved from weak levels and mineral chemicals stayed steady. Management called Q1 exceptional on favourable raw material prices and high DDGS prices, and kept FY27 guidance unchanged while signalling a conservative stance.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue INR426 crore and EBITDA INR81 crore (18% margin); largest contributor to revenue and profit. Installed capacity about 26 crore litres per annum; order book about 19 crore litres.

segments.name: Grain processing (starch, sorbitol, derivatives)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR170 crore and EBITDA INR8 crore in Q1. FY27 guidance is revenue about INR800 crore at about 5% EBITDA margin; no capacity expansion this year.

segments.name: Mineral chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR24 crore and EBITDA INR5 crore (23% margin). Described as stable; no significant capacity expansion planned.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of about INR2,600 crore, unchanged.
Ethanol revenue about INR1,700-1,800 crore on supplies of about 22 crore litres (Q&A cited 21-22 crore litres generating about INR1,800 crore).
Grain processing revenue about INR800 crore; mineral processing about INR100 crore.
Consolidated EBITDA margin about 10-11% and PAT margin about 5-6%; management said it expects to end the year above these margins but is guiding conservatively.
Ethanol debottlenecking to lift utilisation to 100-110% of existing capacity by FY28, with capacity up about 15-20%.
On-site plant at Trident expected to be operational by end of FY27, adding some revenue.
capex_capacity: Majority of recent capex is complete; FY27 focus is on utilisation and cash flow, with only ethanol debottlenecking planned.
Major expansion into specialty and import-substitute chemicals, grain-based derivatives, expected from FY28; products still under evaluation and not yet named.
Starch capacity to be ramped to 100% utilisation by end of FY27; no starch expansion this year.
Capital subsidy of INR5 crore received from Madhya Pradesh in Q2, adjusted against plant and machinery capex.
Ethanol plants at Assam and Madhya Pradesh; four plants in total grinding about 3,000 tonnes of grain per day.
demand_pricing: Government support for ethanol: E20 achieved; E30 targeted by 2030. Management said higher blending beyond 20% may slip 6-12 months because of protests, but E20 will not be rolled back.
Ethanol feedstock mix: about 40% FCI rice, about 50% maize, about 10% broken rice/DDGS.

Maize prices currently INR23-25/kg across plants (Assam 23, Muzaffarnagar 23, Gujarat 24, MP 25); Q1 raw-material costs were favourable and Q2 is seasonally pressured until the Kharif harvest in October-November.
Maize DDGS priced at about INR20-22; stable for about two quarters. DDGS contributes about INR10 per litre of ethanol cost.
Grain processing: domestic starch and derivative prices improved as exports began from Gujarat; sorbitol exported to more than 40 countries. Management expects a sharp YoY improvement in the segment.
Inventory cap of 30-45 days of grain because of storage and working-capital limits, so raw-material volatility is only partly hedged.
Talks on opening ethanol exports to neighbouring countries (Japan, Indonesia mentioned in press); not yet started.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong Q1 ethanol margin a one-off, given FY guidance of about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was exceptional on favourable raw material prices and record DDGS prices. Q2 is seasonally weak, and H2 (Q3-Q4) is usually stronger; guidance is conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Will E30 timelines slip given protests?
qa_highlights.answer: E20 will not be rolled back. E30 is set for 2030, and blending beyond 20% may be delayed by 6-12 months. Steady-state ethanol demand is not expected to be affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ethanol order book and how confident is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: About 19 crore litres already received, with about 2 crore litres more expected. Management is confident of 21-22 crore litres for FY27, generating about INR1,800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw-material price volatility managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Stocking is capped at 30-45 days of grain. Management will stock up during the April and October harvests, and the full-year margin is expected to average out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term ethanol growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity to rise 15-20% through debottlenecking, targeting 100-110% utilisation of existing capacity by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the grain processing underperformance and what is the recovery outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recovery has started with a big YoY margin improvement. Starch capacity is to reach 100% by year-end, with FY27 grain processing EBITDA margin about 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export exposure and hedging approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about INR18 crore, or 5-6% of quarterly turnover. The company does not hedge FX and relies on a natural hedge from equivalent imports.

qa_highlights.question: Were any government subsidies recognised in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Grants and incentives are accounted for on a receipt basis, and nothing was received in Q1. INR5 crore MP capital subsidy was received in Q2 and adjusted against capex.

risks_watch: Q2 seasonal pressure on maize and grain costs before the Kharif harvest; margins may fall short of Q1 levels.
Possible 6-12 month delay to blending beyond E20 because of protests, which could slow incremental ethanol allocations.
Grain processing (starch) remains low-margin, around 5% EBITDA guided, with a recovery still to be proven.
Specialty chemical expansion from FY28 has no named products or capex figure yet.
Ethanol export opening is still at talk stage; timing is uncertain.
Reliance on OMC purchase orders for the 2 crore litre balance not yet received.
key_quotes: So, we are just talking on more conservative guidance we have given for the year, and I hope that we are doing better, we ultimately perform better than what we are guiding.
The increasing blending beyond 20% may be delayed by 6 months to 1 year until these unnecessary social media noise settles down.
R&D process is going on, but we will not be able to give out any name until it has been finalized by the board.
There has been protest, but that is really temporary. The government will not roll back for sure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q1 execution and the FY27 platform, but deliberately conservative on the full-year guidance, which management kept unchanged despite a 14.2% Q1 margin. Management was openly cautious on Q2 raw-material pressure and on ethanol blending beyond E20, which it said may slip 6-12 months; answers on the specialty chemical pipeline and R&D spend were evasive, with no product names or capex figures given.

adds.what: Ethanol debottlenecking lifting capacity about 15-20% (utilisation to 100-110% of existing capacity)
On-site plant at Trident adding some revenue
Specialty and import-substitute chemicals expansion (products not named)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance held at about INR2,600 crore with ethanol supplies of about 22 crore litres, but the capex cycle is largely complete and debottlenecking (15-20% capacity) and specialty chemicals only arrive from FY28, so near-term growth is modest and the Q1 margin spike is called exceptional.
